response: Yes, non-HDL-cholesterol is a better predictor of long-term outcome in patients after acute myocardial infarction compared to LDL-cholesterol. According to the available data, non-attaining non-HDL-C goal predicted major adverse cardiac events (MACE) at long-term follow-up after acute myocardial infarction, whereas non-attaining LDL-C goal was not associated with a higher risk. This suggests that non-HDL-C may be a more suitable target of dyslipidemia treatment than LDL-C in patients after acute myocardial infarction.
